benchmark_type_evidence: we introduce MaXIFE: a comprehensive evaluation benchmark designed to assess instruction-following capabilities across 23 different languages with 1667 verifiable instruction tasks.
brief_description: MaXIFE is a multilingual and cross-lingual instruction-following evaluation benchmark covering 23 languages with 1667 verifiable instruction tasks across 47 instruction subcategories, combining rule-based and model-based evaluation strategies.

datasets.translation_method: Basic Questions: LLM-based translation (GPT-4o and Claude-3.5 Sonnet) followed by native speaker review and correction. Instructions (47 items): professional human translation by native speakers proficient in English. Both underwent multi-round human quality control.
datasets.annotation_method: Data collected via questionnaire from 31 respondents (researchers, native speakers, linguistics experts), then expanded using GPT-4o and Claude-3.5 Sonnet. 795 Basic Questions combined with 47 templatized Instructions (1-3 per question) to form 18,285 parallel evaluation entries.

data_creator_info.creator_affiliation: Waseda University and OPPO AI Center, Shenzhen, China
data_creator_info.evidence: The total number of questionnaire participants was 31 people, of which 19 were male, 12 were female, most people's age distribution was 21-39 years old, and all respondents had high-frequency usage habits of LLMs. The translations were carried out by internal research team members as part of their responsibilities, thus no additional compensation was involved.

datasets.notes: Each of the 23 languages has 795 parallel data points with 1667 total instructions. Evaluation combines Rule-Based (32 instruction subcategories across 7 categories) and Model-Based (15 instruction subcategories across 4 categories) approaches.

translated.evidence: After completing the English version data expansion, we translated the data into 22 other languages. For Basic Questions, given the large volume of 795 items, we used LLM-based translation with GPT-4o and Claude-3.5 Sonnet, followed by native speaker review and correction. For the 47 Instructions, we used professional human translators who were native speakers of the target languages and proficient in English.

native_annotators.evidence: All personnel we hired for instruction data translation and dataset quality control were native speakers of their respective languages, and they possessed near-native English proficiency. Original data collected via questionnaire from 31 respondents including researchers, native speakers, and linguistics experts. However, Basic Questions were LLM-translated with native speaker review, not fully natively authored.

culturally_grounded.evidence: The benchmark is translated from English and focuses on instruction-following mechanics (format, keywords, length, punctuation, etc.) rather than culturally-specific content. The Basic Questions were originally collected in English and expanded using English-language LLMs. While translations were reviewed for naturalness, the tasks test format compliance rather than cultural knowledge.

MaXIFE.annotation_quality_notes: Three-round quality control: (1) content rationality and accuracy, (2) language expression naturalness reviewed by native speakers, (3) parallel consistency across language versions. Human-model evaluation consistency rates: 97.3% (high-resource), 95.2% (medium-resource), 94.6% (low-resource).

datasets_from_scratch_no_english_source.evidence: The entire dataset is constructed from English source data. Basic Questions were first created in English, then translated to 22 other languages.

datasets_translated_from_english.evidence: After completing the English version data expansion, we translated the data into 22 other languages.

details.notes: The benchmark tests instruction-following mechanics (format, keywords, length, repetition, punctuation, citation, emoji, style, tone, content, language_switch) rather than culturally-grounded knowledge. While translations were checked for naturalness and language-specific features (e.g., Bengali numerals, CJK full-width punctuation), the tasks themselves are not culturally grounded.

all_annotators_native_speakers.evidence: All personnel we hired for instruction data translation and dataset quality control were native speakers of their respective languages, and they possessed near-native English proficiency. We invited native speakers to review instructions in each language, ensuring expressions adhered to language conventions.

annotator_workforce.compensation_details: The translations were carried out by internal research team members as part of their responsibilities, thus no additional compensation was involved.
annotator_workforce.evidence: The total number of questionnaire participants was 31 people, of which 19 were male, 12 were female, most people's age distribution was 21-39 years old, and all respondents had high-frequency usage habits of LLMs.

cultural_flags.english_centricity_notes: The benchmark is entirely English-centric in construction: all Basic Questions and Instructions were created in English first and then translated. The evaluation framework extends IFEval (an English-only benchmark) to 23 languages. While language-specific evaluation rules were developed (e.g., for word counting, keyword matching, punctuation), the underlying task design and content originate from English.

notably_excluded: Most of Africa beyond Zulu and Malagasy
Indigenous languages of North America and Australia
geographic_representation.evidence: MaXIFE covers 23 languages spanning Indo-European (8), Austronesian (4), Dravidian (2), Turkic (2), Sino-Tibetan (1), Japonic (1), Koreanic (1), Kartvelian (1), Niger-Congo (1), and Quechuan (1) families.
